one_liner: QuickBooks offers a REST/GraphQL API with OAuth 2.0 authentication and free sandbox access.
gating_notes: Create an app on the Intuit Developer Portal to obtain client ID/secret and sandbox credentials.
oauth_details: Use OAuth 2.0 to obtain an authorization code, exchange it for an access token, then include the token as a Bearer header in API requests.

auth_methods.quote: Use the [OAuth 2.0 protocol] to implement authentication and authorization. Authorization is essential for both testing via sandbox companies and production apps.

primary_auth.quote: If users grant permission, our Intuit OAuth 2.0 Server sends an authorization code back to your app.

credential_access.quote: Yes. The first step is to create an app on the Intuit Developer Platform. This generates credentials you'll use to connect to the Intuit OAuth 2.0 server.

api_type.quote: The QuickBooks Online Accounting API uses both the REST framework and GraphQL.

api_breadth.quote: Intuit announced the App Partner Program, which introduces platform service fees for developers based on a tiered model.

existing_mcp.note: Multiple sources confirm that Intuit has published an official, open-source QuickBooks Online MCP server on GitHub, which was previously unknown.
